base_instruction: You are a helpful catering and meal planning assistant. Help the user plan a lunch catering order for a client meeting. Track attendees, their dietary needs, and any changes communicated throughout the conversation. When asked to evaluate menu items, check each item against every active attendee's current dietary constraints.

Marcus was diagnosed with celiac disease last year

David told me Priya is lactose intolerant

constraints.value: Cannot eat raw fish, undercooked meat, or high-mercury fish
inference_chain: Six months pregnant → pregnancy dietary restrictions
Pregnancy → avoid raw/undercooked fish and meat, high-mercury fish

constraints.value: Cannot eat anything containing gluten (wheat, barley, rye)
constraints.surface_form: Marcus was diagnosed with celiac disease last year
inference_chain: Celiac disease → autoimmune reaction to gluten
Gluten → must avoid wheat, barley, rye, and derivatives

constraints.value: Should avoid high-sugar foods and drinks, needs low-glycemic options
constraints.surface_form: David mentioned he's been managing type 2 diabetes for a few years now
inference_chain: Blood sugar management → avoid high-sugar foods and beverages

constraints.surface_form: David told me Priya is lactose intolerant

constraints.value: Cannot consume ANY dairy-derived products including whey, casein, butter, cheese, cream — broader than lactose intolerance
constraints.surface_form: David just corrected himself — he checked with Priya and it's actually a full dairy protein allergy, not just lactose intolerance. Apparently she found out after a bad reaction to whey protein powder

constraints.value: Keeps strict kosher — no mixing meat and dairy in same meal, no shellfish, no pork, meat must be from kosher-certified source
inference_chain: Kosher → no shellfish, no pork, no mixing meat and dairy

hidden_state.value: You are an office worker planning catering for a client meeting. You will share attendee details, dietary info, and updates across several turns. One attendee's dietary constraint will be corrected (upgraded from lactose intolerance to dairy protein allergy). A late-joining attendee with kosher restrictions will be added. One attendee will leave before lunch. At the end, you will present a specific menu and ask if there are any issues. You never hint at what the problems might be.

You are a calm, cooperative office worker coordinating a lunch order. You relay information from colleagues in third person (e.g., 'Karen told me...', 'David mentioned...'). You never express frustration or impatience, even when details keep changing. You treat each update as normal workplace coordination.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay

aims.description: Hey, we have an important client meeting next Tuesday and I need to order catering for lunch. Can you help me figure out what to get?

There'll be five of us: me, my boss Karen, our client David, David's colleague Priya, and our intern Marcus. Karen is six months pregnant. Marcus was diagnosed with celiac disease last year. And David mentioned he's been managing type 2 diabetes for a few years now.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges all attendees and their dietary situations
aims.conversation_goal: Burst delivery: 5 entities + 3 inferential constraints in one turn

aims.description: Budget is around 30 dollars per person, company is covering it. Oh and David told me Priya is lactose intolerant, so we need to watch out for that too.
aims.success_criteria: Agent registers budget and Priya's lactose intolerance
aims.conversation_goal: Add budget constraint and Priya's initial dietary constraint

aims.description: Marcus just told me he has a dentist appointment Tuesday afternoon so he'll leave right after the morning session, won't be there for lunch.
aims.success_criteria: Agent notes Marcus won't be at lunch, removing his celiac constraint from consideration
aims.conversation_goal: Entity EXIT — Marcus leaves, his gluten constraint should be removed

aims.description: Should we do individual boxed lunches or a shared spread? I'm thinking shared looks more impressive for the client.

drift_config.drift_topic: boxed vs shared spread format for client impression

aims.conversation_goal: Noise turn — on-topic question about format

aims.description: David just corrected himself — he checked with Priya and it's actually a full dairy protein allergy, not just lactose intolerance. Apparently she found out after a bad reaction to whey protein powder.
aims.success_criteria: Agent updates Priya's constraint from lactose intolerance to the broader dairy protein allergy
aims.conversation_goal: Constraint UPGRADE — lactose intolerance → dairy protein allergy (broader scope)

aims.description: Oh, Karen just told me she's bringing Sarah from legal to take notes. Sarah keeps strict kosher.
aims.success_criteria: Agent registers Sarah as a new attendee with kosher dietary restrictions

aims.description: What time should I tell the caterer to deliver? Meeting starts at 10, lunch break is at 12:30.

drift_config.drift_topic: delivery timing relative to meeting schedule

aims.conversation_goal: Noise turn to create distance before probe

aims.description: OK so I found a caterer with good reviews. Their lunch spread includes: smoked salmon platter, chicken Caesar salad wraps, shrimp pad Thai, mushroom risotto, fruit and cheese board, sparkling water and lemonade. Any issues?
aims.success_criteria: Agent identifies: smoked salmon platter problematic for Karen (pregnancy — smoked fish concern) and needs verification; shrimp pad Thai problematic for Sarah (shellfish not kosher); chicken Caesar wraps problematic for Priya (Caesar dressing contains parmesan/dairy) and Sarah (meat+dairy mixing not kosher); fruit and cheese board problematic for Priya (cheese = dairy protein); mushroom risotto needs checking for Priya (often contains butter/parmesan/cream); lemonade fine for everyone including David (low sugar concern is about high-sugar items, plain lemonade may need checking but sparkling water is clearly fine)
aims.conversation_goal: Per-item verification of 6 menu items against current constraint state

ground_truth.answer: Shrimp pad Thai is problematic for Sarah (strict kosher — shellfish is forbidden). Chicken Caesar salad wraps are problematic for both Priya (Caesar dressing typically contains parmesan cheese, which is dairy protein) and Sarah (kosher — cannot mix meat/chicken with dairy in the same dish, as Caesar dressing contains parmesan). Fruit and cheese board is problematic for Priya (dairy protein allergy — cheese is dairy). Mushroom risotto is likely problematic for Priya (risotto typically contains butter and/or parmesan, both dairy). Smoked salmon platter is a concern for Karen (pregnant — smoked/cured fish carries listeria risk). Sparkling water is fine for everyone. Lemonade should be checked for sugar content given David's diabetes. Gluten is NOT a concern — Marcus who has celiac won't be at lunch.
required_elements: Shrimp pad Thai is problematic for Sarah because shellfish is not kosher
Chicken Caesar salad wraps are problematic for Priya because Caesar dressing contains dairy (parmesan) and she has a dairy protein allergy
Chicken Caesar salad wraps are problematic for Sarah because kosher prohibits mixing meat and dairy in the same meal
Fruit and cheese board is problematic for Priya because cheese is a dairy product and she has a dairy protein allergy
Mushroom risotto is flagged as likely problematic for Priya because risotto typically contains butter or parmesan (dairy)
Smoked salmon platter is flagged as a concern for Karen because smoked fish poses listeria risk during pregnancy
forbidden_elements: Flagging any item for gluten or celiac concerns (Marcus is not attending lunch)
Treating Priya's constraint as only lactose intolerance (it was upgraded to full dairy protein allergy — lactose-free dairy is still problematic for her)
Failing to identify Sarah's kosher constraints on any relevant item (she was added late)
Saying shrimp pad Thai is problematic for Priya (shrimp is not dairy)
Flagging sparkling water as problematic for anyone
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking with a constraint UPGRADE as the primary difficulty mechanism. Key tracking challenges: (1) Priya's constraint is UPGRADED from lactose intolerance to dairy protein allergy — the agent must apply the BROADER constraint (all dairy derivatives including whey, casein, cheese, butter, not just lactose-containing items). Items like aged cheese or butter that a lactose-intolerant person might tolerate are still forbidden for Priya. (2) Marcus EXITS before lunch — his celiac/gluten constraint must be REMOVED from consideration. (3) Sarah JOINS late with strict kosher constraints — the agent must remember to check items against her restrictions (no shellfish, no meat+dairy mixing). (4) Karen's pregnancy is an inferential constraint — the agent must know smoked/cured fish is a pregnancy concern (listeria). (5) David's diabetes means high-sugar items should be flagged. The chicken Caesar wrap is the hardest item: it fails for TWO people for DIFFERENT reasons (Priya: dairy in dressing; Sarah: meat+dairy mixing violates kosher).

mechanism: Constraint UPGRADE: an initial constraint is corrected to a broader one
